# SPD-063 — Bash hook: program-naming config keys in the config files git reads with nothing set on the line

## Brief
SPD-047 closes the alias half of every unreadable config file at once: an alias can only introduce a verb git does not have, so an unknown verb is refused. The other half of SPD-046's class is still open in the files git finds by itself, with no variable and no -C on the line: core.pager, core.sshCommand, core.hooksPath, diff.external and the rest run a program under a real, allowed verb. Three sources: the user's ~/.gitconfig (a member may write it -- it lies outside every registered project, so edit_reason returns no reason and the path rule never applies), the system config, and the .git/config of a repository inside a checkout the ledger knows, which a member can create under its own deliverable globs (`git -C tests/fake status` resolves inside the home and stays silent by design, since SPD-047 only refuses targets outside every known checkout). A fix with evidence behind it: before allowing a member's git call, run `git config --list --show-scope --name-only` in the target checkout with the hook's sanitised environment and hold every key in force to SPD-046's inert allowlist (git_config_key_allowed), refusing with the scope and key named; or, narrower, have the edit hook refuse a member writing any file named .gitconfig, .git/config or git/config anywhere, deliverables included.

Evidence: bin/spud_ledger.py edit_reason (about line 6209): 'inside = project_paths(...); if not inside: return None, None' -- a path outside every registered project is refused to nobody, so a member's Write to ~/.gitconfig is allowed. analyse_command on the new tree: 'git -C tests/fake status' gives [('git', ('status', None)), ('git-repo', ('-C tests/fake', 'tests/fake', ...))] and git_repo_outside resolves tests/fake inside the home, so it stays silent; 'git status' with a planted ~/.gitconfig gives only ('git', ('status', None)). SPD-046's probes already showed core.pager, core.sshCommand, diff.external and GIT_SSH_COMMAND each run the named program under an allowed verb; SPD-047's probes showed git reads ~/.gitconfig, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config and the target repository's .git/config without anything on the line pointing at them.

## Size, persona and model decision
Cluster A of Eric's batch of 2026-09-15, with SPD-064, same engineer on opus. Both fixes from the brief: the edit hook refuses a member writing a file named .gitconfig, .git/config or git/config anywhere, deliverables included; and a member's git call is held to SPD-046's allowlist for the program-naming keys in force in the target repository's local and worktree scopes, read from git and cached under the config files' stat fingerprints since the hook path never imports subprocess (SPD-016). The system and global scopes are Eric's own (credential.helper is in force on this Mac at the system scope) and SPD-064 closes a member's writes to them.

## Outcome
Landed on main as 350e52b with SPD-064, suite 732 OK. Any .gitconfig, .git/config, .git/config.worktree or git/config is refused to every member, deliverables included. git config's subcommands are read as git 2.46 spells them: git config edit, a write that had slipped through, is refused, and git config get and --get-urlmatch are reads again. Before a member's git call the target repository's local and worktree keys are read once and cached under the config files' stat fingerprint (cold 13 ms, warm 0.04 ms); keys that name a program and are not in SPD-046's inert allowlist refuse the call with the scope and key named. Spud accepted a program-naming classifier over a default-deny of every local key, since ordinary local keys in this checkout and BadTakes sit outside the allowlist; a repository using git-lfs would refuse every member git call there, by design.
